Write BDD spec files for THREE stories SEQUENTIALLY in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm: 848 (instant quote), 849 (accept & book), 850 (client portal).

MCP note: on "No session_id available" errors add explicit session_id "b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8"; if MCP hangs >2 min, message me and wait; timed-out writes often commit server-side — verify with a read before re-writing.

Per story: start_task requirement_name="bdd_specs_exist", entity_type="story", entity_id="<id>", follow its prompt (it gives criteria, scenarios, file paths, spec templates). Then evaluate_task. Message me one line per story.

CRITICAL project conventions (learned over 100 existing spex — read 2-3 files under test/spex/836_*/ first as reference):
- One file per criterion: test/spex/<story>_<slug>/criterion_<id>_<slug>_spex.exs; module CleanerCrmSpex.Story<id>.Criterion<cid>Spex; `use CleanerCrmSpex.Case`; given_/when_/then_ blocks returning {:ok, context}.

NO if/case/cond in tests.
- Drive the REAL surface with LiveViewTest (live/render_click/render_change/render_submit/follow_redirect). phx-change inputs must be targeted inside forms. HEEx escapes apostrophes — avoid contractions in asserted copy. UUID regexes: [0-9a-f-]+.
- The app modules are CleanerCrm/CleanerCrmWeb.

ROUTE CONTRACT (implementation will match this — use exactly these):
- GET /book — public instant-quote calculator (unauthenticated LiveView CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote)
- GET /book/accept/:token — quote acceptance flow (BookingLive.Accept; lead's acceptance token)
- GET /portal/access/:token — magic-link entry; sets portal session and redirects to /portal
- GET /portal — PortalLive.Home (upcoming visits + assigned cleaner + history w/ proof-of-work); unauthorized (no portal session) redirects to a request-link page
- Stripe interactions go through the existing StripeGateway Test adapter (card capture = setup intent token param is acceptable at spex level).

The specs SHOULD FAIL initially (routes don't exist yet) — the evaluator checks existence/compilation/validity, not green. They must COMPILE: run `mix compile` (test env via MIX_ENV=test mix compile) and fix syntax; run `PORT=4002 mix spex test/spex/<dir>` once to confirm failures are missing-feature failures, not compile errors.

Final response: one line per story (file count, compile status). Under 60 words.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7155Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7155 — Client with no card on file pays via payment link

  As in criterion 7154, job completion and invoice generation are
  seeded via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` (covered end-to-end by
  criterion 7153) so this spec can focus on the payment-link
  collection path.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "collecting payment via a payment link when no card is on file" do
    scenario "client with no card on file pays via payment link" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client has no card on file", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{card_on_file: false})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client, client)}
      end

      given_ "an invoice exists for that client's completed job", context do
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, context.client)
        invoice = Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{amount: job.agreed_price})

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{job: job, invoice: invoice})}
      end

      when_ "the owner sends the invoice as a payment link and the client pays it online",
            context do
        {:ok, invoice_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices/#{context.invoice.id}")

        html_after_send =
          invoice_live
          |> element("[data-test='send-payment-link-button']")
          |> render_click()

        [_, payment_path] = Regex.run(~r{href="(/pay/[^"]+)"}, html_after_send)

        client_conn =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> post(payment_path, %{"payment_method" => "pm_card_visa", "save_card" => "true"})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client_conn, client_conn)}
      end

      then_ "the invoice is collected", context do
        assert Phoenix.ConnTest.html_response(context.client_conn, 200) =~ "Payment received"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the client's card can be saved for next time", context do
        assert Phoenix.ConnTest.html_response(context.client_conn, 200) =~ "save your card"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7153Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7153 — Completing a job generates its invoice
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "marking a job complete generates its invoice" do
    scenario "completing a job generates its invoice" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a scheduled job has an agreed price of $150", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner marks the job complete", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      then_ "the job is shown as complete to the cleaner", context do
        assert render(context.job_live) =~ "Complete"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "an invoice for $150 appears in the owner's billing queue", context do
        {:ok, _invoices_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices")

        assert html =~ context.client.name
        assert html =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false,
          email: "client#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    attrs = Enum.into(attrs, %{})
    start_time = Map.get(attrs, :start_time, ~T[09:00:00])

    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: start_time,
          # Some specs override `start_time` alone (e.g. pinning it to a
          # lead-time boundary) without overriding `end_time` — a fixed
          # `~T[11:00:00]` default would then land before an overridden
          # start_time and fail the "end after start" changeset check.
          end_time: default_end_time(start_time)
        })
      )

    # Notifications (story 837) — the automatic reminder trigger is a
    # periodic Oban-cron scan in production (see the background-jobs
    # ADR); nothing about creating a job through this fixture would
    # otherwise run that scan within a spec's lifetime. Running it here
    # is a no-op for every job outside its owning account's configured
    # lead-time window (and a no-op entirely for accounts that never
    # configured reminders), so it's safe for every other story's jobs
    # while making story 837's own boundary-timed fixtures deterministic.
    CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()

    job
  end

  # `given_` blocks bind `scope` from `user_scope_fixture/1` *before*
  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  # Two hours after `start_time`, unless that would wrap past midnight
  # (into an earlier clock time), in which case the day just ends there.
  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, 2 * 3600, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story835.Criterion7119Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 835 — Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing
  Criterion 7119 — Owner quotes a phone lead without visiting the
  property: a quote can be built and sent entirely from client-supplied
  details, with no in-person walkthrough required first.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  setup context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
    conn = CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

    {:ok, conn: conn, user: user, account: account}
  end

  spex "owner quotes a phone lead without visiting the property" do
    scenario "a complete priced quote is sent without scheduling a site visit" do
      given_ "a lead has given the owner their room count and square footage over the phone",
             context do
        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='rate-card-form']",
          rate_card: %{per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 5000, per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: 3000}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the owner builds a quote entering those details from their device", context do
        context.quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
          quote: %{
            client_name: "Dana Prescott",
            client_phone: "555-0142",
            pricing_model: "per_room",
            bedroom_count: 3,
            bathroom_count: 1
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        context.quote_live
        |> element("[data-test='send-quote-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner can produce and send a complete priced quote without scheduling a site visit",
            context do
        path = assert_patch(context.quote_live)
        {:ok, sent_live, html} = live(context.conn, path)

        assert html =~ "$180.00"
        assert has_element?(sent_live, "[data-test='quote-status']", "Sent")
        refute html =~ "Schedule a site visit"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Quotes built from the account's rate card using per-room, per-sqft,
4	  or hourly pricing models.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. A quote is
7	  built up in memory (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`) and only ever
8	  persisted at the moment it's sent — `send_quote/3` freezes the rate
9	  card's current rates into the quote's line items, so later rate-card
10	  edits never alter an already-sent quote.
11	  """
12	
13	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
14	
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
16	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
17	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
18	  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, QuoteItem, RateCard, Pricing}
19	
20	  ## Rate card
21	
22	  @doc """
23	  Returns the account's rate card, creating a blank one on first use.
24	  """
25	  def get_or_create_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
26	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
27	    case Repo.get_by(RateCard, account_id: account_id) do
28	      nil -> Repo.insert!(%RateCard{account_id: account_id})
29	      rate_card -> rate_card
30	    end
31	  end
32	
33	  def change_rate_card(%Scope{}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs \\ %{}) do
34	    RateCard.changeset(rate_card, attrs)
35	  end
36	
37	  def update_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs)
38	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
39	    rate_card
40	    |> RateCard.changeset(attrs)
41	    |> Repo.update()
42	  end
43	
44	  ## Quotes
45	
46	  def change_quote(%Scope{}, %Quote{} = quote, attrs \\ %{}) do
47	    Quote.changeset(quote, attrs)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting do
  @moduledoc """
  Quotes built from the account's rate card using per-room, per-sqft,
  or hourly pricing models.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. A quote is
  built up in memory (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`) and only ever
  persisted at the moment it's sent — `send_quote/3` freezes the rate
  card's current rates into the quote's line items, so later rate-card
  edits never alter an already-sent quote.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, QuoteItem, RateCard, Pricing}

  ## Rate card

  @doc """
  Returns the account's rate card, creating a blank one on first use.
  """
  def get_or_create_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(RateCard, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> Repo.insert!(%RateCard{account_id: account_id})
      rate_card -> rate_card
    end
  end

  def change_rate_card(%Scope{}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RateCard.changeset(rate_card, attrs)
  end

  def update_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    rate_card
    |> RateCard.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Quotes

  def change_quote(%Scope{}, %Quote{} = quote, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Quote.changeset(quote, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists the account's quotes, most recently sent first.
  """
  def list_quotes(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Quote
    |> where([q], q.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([q], desc: q.inserted_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_quote!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Quote
    |> where([q], q.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(:quote_items)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Finalizes a draft quote against the current rate card: prices every
  line item, then inserts the quote and its `CleanerCrm.Quoting.QuoteItem`s
  together, freezing the rates and amounts at this moment.

  Refuses with `{:error, :not_finalizable}` when any priced line item
  is missing a rate on the rate card, or the total isn't positive — a
  sent quote can never be a zero-dollar or partially-rated quote.
  """
  def send_quote(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Quote{} = draft,
        %RateCard{} = rate_card
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    line_items = Pricing.line_items(rate_card, draft)

    if Pricing.finalizable?(line_items) do
      insert_sent_quote(scope, account_id, draft, line_items)
    else
      {:error, :not_finalizable}
    end
  end

  defp insert_sent_quote(scope, account_id, draft, line_items) do
    quote_attrs = %{
      client_id: draft.client_id,
      client_name: draft.client_name,
      client_phone: draft.client_phone,
      pricing_model: draft.pricing_model,
      bedroom_count: draft.bedroom_count,
      bathroom_count: draft.bathroom_count,
      square_feet: draft.square_feet,
      hours: draft.hours,
      status: :sent,
      total_cents: Pricing.total_cents(line_items),
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    }

    Repo.transaction(fn ->
      with {:ok, quote} <-
             %Quote{account_id: account_id} |> Quote.changeset(quote_attrs) |> Repo.insert(),
           {:ok, _items} <- insert_quote_items(quote, line_items) do
        Recorder.record(scope, "quote_sent", "Quote", quote.id, %{}, %{
          "total_cents" => quote.total_cents
        })

        quote
      else
        {:error, changeset} -> Repo.rollback(changeset)
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_quote_items(quote, line_items) do
    Enum.reduce_while(line_items, {:ok, []}, fn line_item, {:ok, acc} ->
      case %QuoteItem{quote_id: quote.id} |> QuoteItem.changeset(line_item) |> Repo.insert() do
        {:ok, quote_item} -> {:cont, {:ok, [quote_item | acc]}}
        {:error, _changeset} = error -> {:halt, error}
      end
    end)
  end
end

      Given a business with a per-room rate card and a visitor on the public quote page
      When the visitor selects a service type, bedroom count, and bathroom count without entering a name, email, or phone
      Then a real price computed from the rate card is displayed immediately

    Scenario: Building a quote by square footage instead of room counts
      Given a business with a per-square-foot rate card
      When the visitor enters the home's square footage and a service type
      Then the displayed price is computed using the per-square-foot rate

  Rule: The displayed price updates immediately as the customer changes any input (rooms, bathrooms, square footage, frequency, add-ons).
    Scenario: Changing any input recomputes the total live
      Given a quote is currently displayed for a 2-bedroom home
      When the visitor changes the bedroom count to 3
      Then the displayed price updates immediately to reflect the new bedroom count without a page reload

  Rule: Selecting a recurring frequency applies the rate card's configured discount to the subtotal.
    Scenario: Selecting bi-weekly frequency applies the recurring discount
      Given a one-time quote subtotal has been computed
      When the visitor changes the frequency to bi-weekly
      Then the displayed total is reduced by the rate card's configured bi-weekly discount

  Rule: If the client's inputs fall outside what the business's rate card can price, the form shows a clear message and withholds a price rather than guessing or showing a wrong number.

      Given a business's rate card has no configured price for a selected service type and size combination
      When the visitor selects that unsupported combination
      Then the form shows a clear "can't price this yet, request a custom quote" message instead of displaying $0 or a guessed price

  Rule: Each selected add-on adds its configured amount to the running total.

      Given a base quote is displayed with no add-ons selected
      When the visitor selects "inside fridge" and "interior windows" add-ons
      Then the running total increases by the sum of both add-ons' configured amounts

  Rule: The quoted price is the same number that carries through to acceptance and booking — no hidden fees are added afterward.

      Given a visitor sees an instant quote total of $195 in integer cents
      When they proceed to the accept-and-book step without changing any selections
      Then the total shown at acceptance is exactly $195 with no added fees

## Accept a quote and book online with card on file (ID: 849)

As a cleaning client, I want to accept my quote online — pick a slot, agree to the cancellation policy, and put a card on file — so that booking is done in minutes and the price I saw is the price I'm charged. (Research: Jobber captures cards at quote acceptance; capturing policy agreement at booking is best practice; bait-and-switch pricing is a top category complaint — customer-side.md §1, §2)

**Acceptance Criteria:** 8 total, 0 verified

- [ ] Client selects an open slot and proceeds to review (criterion 7228)
- [ ] Selected slot becomes unavailable before confirmation (criterion 7230)
- [ ] Client views and agrees to the cancellation policy before confirming (criterion 7231)
- [ ] Booking is blocked without cancellation policy agreement (criterion 7232)
- [ ] Client enters a valid card and the booking confirms (criterion 7233)
- [ ] Payment gateway declines the card (criterion 7234)
- [ ] Card is authorized for the exact quoted amount (criterion 7235)
- [ ] Confirmed booking appears for client and business with portal access (criterion 7236)

Feature: Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  As a cleaning client, I want to accept my quote online — pick a slot, agree to the cancellation policy, and put a card on file — so that booking is done in minutes and the price I saw is the price I'm charged. (Research: Jobber captures cards at quote acceptance; capturing policy agreement at booking is best practice; bait-and-switch pricing is a top category complaint — customer-side.md §1, §2)
  Rule: Booking requires an available time slot to be selected before the client can confirm.
    Scenario: Client selects an open slot and proceeds to review
      Given a client has an accepted instant quote and the business has open slots
      When the client selects an available date and time
      Then the booking flow proceeds to cancellation policy and payment

    Scenario: Selected slot becomes unavailable before confirmation
      Given a client has selected a time slot but another booking claims it first
      When the client attempts to confirm the booking
      Then the booking is blocked with a message to pick another slot and no charge is made

  Rule: The client must explicitly agree to the cancellation policy — the 24-hour notice window and the fee — before the booking can be confirmed.
    Scenario: Client views and agrees to the cancellation policy before confirming
      Given the client has selected a slot and reached the confirmation step
      When the cancellation policy (24-hour notice and fee) is displayed and the client checks agreement
      Then the client is allowed to proceed to payment

    Scenario: Booking is blocked without cancellation policy agreement
      Given the client has selected a slot and reached the confirmation step
      When the client tries to confirm without checking the cancellation policy agreement
      Then the booking is not confirmed and the client is prompted to agree first

  Rule: A valid payment card must be captured and stored on file via the payment gateway before the booking is confirmed.
    Scenario: Client enters a valid card and the booking confirms
      Given the client has agreed to the cancellation policy
      When the client enters a valid card and the payment gateway accepts it
      Then the card is stored on file and the booking is confirmed

    Scenario: Payment gateway declines the card
      Given the client has agreed to the cancellation policy and submitted a card
      When the payment gateway declines the card
      Then the booking is not confirmed and the client is prompted to retry with a different card

  Rule: Confirming the booking converts the accepted quote into a scheduled job visible to both the client and the business, and sends the client a confirmation with portal access.
    Scenario: Confirmed booking appears for client and business with portal access
      Given the booking has been confirmed with card on file
      When the confirmation completes
      Then the visit appears as scheduled for both the business and the client, and the client receives a confirmation containing a magic-link to their portal

  Rule: The amount authorized on the client's card at booking is exactly the quoted price the client saw, in integer cents — the same number later invoiced at job completion, with no adjustment.
    Scenario: Card is authorized for the exact quoted amount
      Given the client saw an instant quote total of $195 in integer cents
      When the client completes booking with a valid card
      Then the gateway authorizes exactly $195 with no added fee

As a cleaning client, I want a portal showing my upcoming visits with the named, photo-identified cleaner assigned, plus my service history with checklist results and before/after photos, so that I know who is entering my home and can see exactly what I paid for. (Research: trust is the #1 gate — 73% of bad experiences trace to trust; Jobber's Client Hub shows assigned-team photos for this reason — customer-side.md §1, §2)

- [ ] Expired or invalid magic link denies access (criterion 7252)

- [ ] Reassigning the cleaner updates what the client sees (criterion 7254)
- [ ] Unassigned upcoming visit shows a placeholder (criterion 7255)
- [ ] Completed visit in history shows checklist and before/after photos (criterion 7256)
- [ ] Portal proof-of-work matches the invoice's evidence (criterion 7257)

Feature: See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  As a cleaning client, I want a portal showing my upcoming visits with the named, photo-identified cleaner assigned, plus my service history with checklist results and before/after photos, so that I know who is entering my home and can see exactly what I paid for. (Research: trust is the #1 gate — 73% of bad experiences trace to trust; Jobber's Client Hub shows assigned-team photos for this reason — customer-side.md §1, §2)
  Rule: Portal access is granted via a unique magic-link token tied to the client — there is no username/password login.
    Scenario: Client opens the portal via a valid magic link
      Given a client has been sent a magic-link token for their portal
      When the client follows the link
      Then the portal opens showing their upcoming visits and service history without requiring a password

    Scenario: Expired or invalid magic link denies access
      Given a client's magic-link token has expired or is invalid
      When the client follows the link
      Then access to the portal is denied and the client is offered a way to request a fresh link

  Rule: Upcoming visits display the date/time and the named, photo-identified cleaner assigned to that visit.
    Scenario: Upcoming visit shows the assigned cleaner's name and photo
      Given a client has an upcoming visit with a cleaner assigned
      When the client views the portal
      Then the visit shows the date/time along with the cleaner's name and photo

    Scenario: Reassigning the cleaner updates what the client sees
      Given a client's upcoming visit currently shows Cleaner A
      When the business reassigns the visit to Cleaner B
      Then the client's portal shows Cleaner B's name and photo the next time it is viewed

  Rule: A visit with no cleaner assigned yet shows a clear "not yet assigned" state instead of a blank or broken cleaner card.
    Scenario: Unassigned upcoming visit shows a placeholder
      Given a client has an upcoming visit that has no cleaner assigned yet
      When the client views the portal
      Then the visit shows a "cleaner not yet assigned" placeholder instead of a blank or broken card

  Rule: Completed visits show the finished checklist results and before/after photos as proof-of-work in the client's service history.
    Scenario: Completed visit in history shows checklist and before/after photos
      Given a client has a past visit that was completed with a finished checklist and before/after photos
      When the client views that visit in their service history
      Then the checklist results and before/after photos are displayed

  Rule: The proof-of-work shown in the portal for a completed visit is the same evidence attached to that visit's invoice.
    Scenario: Portal proof-of-work matches the invoice's evidence
      Given a completed visit has an invoice with attached checklist and photos as dispute evidence
      When the client views that same visit in the portal
      Then the checklist and photos shown match exactly what is attached to the invoice

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Hides the Stripe API behind two operations: submitting a charge as a
4	  PaymentIntent, and verifying an inbound webhook request. `CleanerCrm.Billing`
5	  calls through the configured adapter — `Test` in test (see
6	  `config/test.exs`), `Live` everywhere else — so a test never reaches
7	  the real Stripe API, and the real adapter is the only one that ever
8	  checks a webhook signature.
9	
10	  Configure the adapter and (for `Live`) credentials with:
11	
12	      config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway,
13	        adapter: CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live,
14	        secret_key: System.get_env("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"),
15	        webhook_secret: System.get_env("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET")
16	  """
17	
18	  @type charge_params :: %{
19	          required(:amount_cents) => pos_integer(),
20	          required(:payment_method) => String.t(),
21	          optional(:off_session) => boolean(),
22	          optional(:metadata) => map()
23	        }
24	
25	  @callback create_payment_intent(charge_params()) ::
26	              {:ok, %{id: String.t(), status: String.t()}} | {:error, map()}
27	
28	  @callback verify_webhook_event(Plug.Conn.t()) :: {:ok, map()} | {:error, atom()}
29	
30	  def create_payment_intent(params), do: adapter().create_payment_intent(params)
31	
32	  def verify_webhook_event(conn), do: adapter().verify_webhook_event(conn)
33	
34	  defp adapter do
35	    :cleaner_crm
36	    |> Application.get_env(__MODULE__, [])
37	    |> Keyword.get(:adapter, __MODULE__.Live)
38	  end
39	end
40

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while some spex drive the same form with a
  # `scheduled_date` override instead (matching the schema field name
  # directly). The form carries a second, always-blank
  # `job[scheduled_date]` field purely as a landing pad for that
  # override key (`Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` requires an override's
  # key to match a real field name in the form). Whichever one arrives
  # non-blank wins; `scheduled_date` takes precedence when both do,
  # since a still-blank landing pad means only `date` was ever touched.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")

  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

These are specifications of acceptance criteria, not regression tests
of existing behavior. A scenario is a mechanical translation of the

today.

**Failing on first run is the expected outcome.** Unsatisfied criteria

the implementation. You do **not** need the scenarios to pass for
this task to succeed.

worry about turning it green.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared givens for Cleaner CRM BDD specs.

  Consumer spex modules pull these in with a plain Elixir `import`:

      import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

      scenario "..." do
        given_ :logged_in_owner_with_account
      end

  | Name | Produces | Requires |
  |---|---|---|
  | `:logged_in_owner_with_account` | `context.conn` (authenticated), `context.user`, `context.scope`, `context.account` | `context.conn` |
  """

  use SexySpex.Givens

  import Phoenix.ConnTest
  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

  register_given :logged_in_owner_with_account, context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture() |> Fixtures.set_password()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, login_live, _html} = live(context.conn, "/users/log-in")

    form =
      form(login_live, "#login_form_password",
        user: %{
          email: user.email,
          password: Fixtures.valid_user_password(),
          remember_me: true
        }
      )

    conn = submit_form(form, context.conn)

    {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
  end
end

# BDD Spec Plan — Cleaner CRM

How BDD specs work in *this* project. The framework docs
(`philosophy.md`, `boundaries.md`, `writing_a_spex.md` in the harness
knowledge base) cover the generic rules; this file names the concrete
surfaces, fixtures, and anti-patterns for Cleaner CRM.

## Public surfaces a spec may drive

Specs act through LiveView routes (via `Phoenix.LiveViewTest`) and the
public controllers. Concretely:

**Office/admin side (owner persona):**
- `CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.*` — `/clients`, client + property + access management (story 832)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Board` — `/schedule`, weekly dispatch board (833, 834, 846)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.*` — `/quotes`, quote builder (835)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.*` — `/invoices` (836)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive` — reminder settings + delivery log (837)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetLive` — time review + payroll export (838)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.*` — job review + scorecards (839)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.AuditLive` — audit trail (840)

**Cleaner field side (cleaner persona):**
- `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Today` — day view + change alerts (841, 843)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job` — checklist, photos, clock in/out, incident reports (842, 844, 845)

**Public (unauthenticated) surfaces:**
- `CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController` — payment-link pages (836)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderController` — reminder confirm/reschedule links (837)
- Auth: `/users/register`, `/users/log-in` LiveViews (generated)

## Fixture inventory (`CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`)

- `user_fixture/1` — confirmed user (owner/office/cleaner depending on attrs)
- `unconfirmed_user_fixture/1` — pre-confirmation user for auth specs
- `user_scope_fixture/0,1` — scope wrapping a user, for seeding deeper state
- `valid_user_password/0`, `set_password/1` — password login in specs
- `account_fixture/2` — a company (tenant) owned by the given scope

Grow this list only when a spec's `given_` needs state whose creation
flow is covered by another spec. Every addition is a sanctioned bypass.

## Legal observable surfaces in `then_`

- LiveView render assertions: `assert render(view) =~ "Job scheduled"`
- LiveView navigation: `assert_patch/2`, `assert_redirect/2`
- Flash content via rendered layout
- Controller responses: `html_response(conn, 200)`, redirects on payment/reminder links
- Email delivery via `Swoosh.TestAssertions` (reminder + invitation emails)
- NOT legal: asserting on Repo rows, context return values, or PubSub
  messages via direct `assert_receive` on internals — observe what a
  user (or webhook peer) can observe.

## Project-specific anti-patterns

- Do not seed `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` jobs in `given_` by calling the
  context — the covered creation flow is the ScheduleLive board / plan
  form. If a spec needs "a scheduled job" as a precondition, either
  drive the UI in `given_` steps or add a sanctioned fixture here first.
- Do not flip `Notification` acknowledgment state directly — the whole
  point of story 843 is the acknowledgment round-trip through
  `FieldLive.Today`.
- Do not stub time by editing rows; recurrence/conflict scenarios pin
  wall-clock via plan dates chosen in the future.
- External HTTP (Stripe, Twilio, Resend, S3) is always cassette- or
  adapter-faked; a spec must never hit a live API.

1	defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Public payment-link pages: a client without a card on file reaches
4	  `/pay/:token` (the link `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show` sends) to
5	  pay an invoice directly, no login required.
6	
7	  ## Dependencies
8	
9	  - `CleanerCrm.Billing`
10	  """
11	
12	  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
13	
14	  alias CleanerCrm.Billing
15	
16	  def show(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
17	    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
18	      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
19	      invoice -> render(conn, :show, invoice: invoice)
20	    end
21	  end
22	
23	  def create(conn, %{"token" => token} = params) do
24	    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
25	      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
26	      invoice -> submit_payment(conn, invoice, params)
27	    end
28	  end
29	
30	  defp submit_payment(conn, invoice, params) do
31	    payment_method = Map.get(params, "payment_method")
32	    save_card = Map.get(params, "save_card") in ["true", "on"]
33	
34	    case Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, payment_method) do
35	      {:ok, updated} ->
36	        render(conn, :paid, invoice: updated, save_card: save_card)
37	
38	      {:error, reason} ->
39	        render(conn, :declined, invoice: invoice, message: decline_message(reason))
40	    end
41	  end
42	
43	  # A genuine card decline gets its own message; anything else (a
44	  # misconfigured or unreachable payment provider) gets a neutral one —
45	  # never blaming the payer's card for what's actually our problem.
46	  defp decline_message(%{"code" => "card_declined"}) do
47	    "Your card was declined. Please try a different payment method or contact us for help."
48	  end
49	
50	  defp decline_message(_reason) do
51	    "We couldn't process your payment right now. Please try again shortly or contact us for help."
52	  end
53	
54	  defp render_not_found(conn) do
55	    conn
56	    |> put_status(:not_found)
57	    |> render(:not_found)
58	  end
59	end
60

  def create(conn, %{"token" => token} = params) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> submit_payment(conn, invoice, params)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(conn, invoice, params) do
    payment_method = Map.get(params, "payment_method")
    save_card = Map.get(params, "save_card") in ["true", "on"]

    case Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, payment_method) do
      {:ok, updated} ->
        render(conn, :paid, invoice: updated, save_card: save_card)

      {:error, reason} ->
        render(conn, :declined, invoice: invoice, message: decline_message(reason))
    end
  end

  # A genuine card decline gets its own message; anything else (a
  # misconfigured or unreachable payment provider) gets a neutral one —
  # never blaming the payer's card for what's actually our problem.
  defp decline_message(%{"code" => "card_declined"}) do
    "Your card was declined. Please try a different payment method or contact us for help."
  end

  defp decline_message(_reason) do
    "We couldn't process your payment right now. Please try again shortly or contact us for help."
  end

  defp render_not_found(conn) do
    conn
    |> put_status(:not_found)
    |> render(:not_found)
  end
end

def generate_for_job(%Scope{}, %Job{agreed_price_cents: nil}), do: {:error, :no_price}

  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{card_on_file: false}, _invoice, _opts),
    do: {:error, :no_card_on_file}

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Charges the given payment method against the invoice reached via its
  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
  """
  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
    end
  end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })
  end

  # Clients doesn't yet persist a real Stripe payment-method/customer id
  # (only the `card_on_file` flag) — this placeholder stands in until a
  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """
  def create_payment_link(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.Builder do @moduledoc """ Builds and sends a quote, with live totals as the owner fills it in. The rate card and quote forms live on the same page: a quote is priced by exactly one model at a time, so switching models drops whatever the previous model's inputs held (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing.fields_for_model/1`). A quote is only ever persisted at the moment it's sent — before that, everything here is in-memory socket state. ## Routes * `/quotes/new` (`:new`) — build and send a new quote. * `/quotes/:id` (`:show`) — a previously sent quote, frozen against later rate-card changes. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Quoting` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Money alias CleanerCrm.Quoting alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Pricing, Quote} @impl true def render(%{live_action: :show} = assigns) do ~H""" <.header> {@quote.client_name || "Unnamed lead"} <:subtitle>{pricing_model_label(@quote.pricing_model)} quote <:actions> <.button navigate={~p"/quotes"} class="btn-sm btn-ghost">Back to Quotes

Status: {status_label(@quote.status)}

Phone: {@quote.client_phone}

  • {item.description} × {item.quantity} @ {Money.format_cents(item.rate_cents)}
    {Money.format_cents(item.amount_cents)}

Total: {Money.format_cents(@quote.total_cents)}

""" end def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> New Quote <:subtitle>Price a job by room, square footage, or hours

Only the visible model's group loses the `hidden` class, and only its inputs carry a `data-test` attribute — the other models' fields are inert without either. --%>
<.input field={@form[:bedroom_count]} type="number" label="Bedrooms" data-test={active_field(@pricing_model, :per_room, "room-bedroom-count-input")} /> <.input field={@form[:bathroom_count]} type="number" label="Bathrooms" data-test={active_field(@pricing_model, :per_room, "room-bathroom-count-input")} />

<.input field={@form[:hours]} type="number" label="Hours" data-test={active_field(@pricing_model, :hourly, "hours-input")} />

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story835.Criterion7120Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 835 — Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing
  Criterion 7120 — Missing rate on the chosen model blocks finalizing:
  a quote cannot be finalized until every line item in the chosen model
  has a rate and the total is greater than zero.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  setup context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
    conn = CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

    {:ok, conn: conn, user: user, account: account}
  end

  spex "missing rate on the chosen model blocks finalizing" do
    scenario "finalizing is blocked and the owner is prompted to set the missing rate" do
      given_ "the owner's rate card has no rate configured for the hourly model", context do
        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the owner builds an hourly quote and tries to finalize it", context do
        context.quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']", quote: %{pricing_model: "hourly", hours: 3})
        |> render_change()

        html =
          context.quote_live
          |> element("[data-test='send-quote-button']")
          |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "finalizing is blocked and the owner is prompted to set the missing rate before sending, preventing a zero-dollar quote",
            context do
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='hours-input'][value='3']")
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='missing-rate-warning']")
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$0.00")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7158Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7158 — Invoice marked paid on provider confirmation
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "marking an invoice paid only on provider confirmation" do
    scenario "invoice marked paid on provider confirmation" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "an invoice charge has been submitted to the payment provider", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{card_on_file: true})
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)

        invoice =
          Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{
            amount: job.agreed_price,
            status: :charge_pending,
            stripe_payment_intent_id: "pi_test_succeeded_123"
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, invoice: invoice})}
      end

      when_ "the provider confirms the charge succeeded", context do
        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => context.invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id,
              "metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => to_string(context.invoice.id)}
            }
          }
        }

        response =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
          |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
          |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :webhook_response, response)}
      end

      then_ "the invoice is marked paid", context do
        {:ok, _invoice_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices/#{context.invoice.id}")

        assert html =~ "Paid"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner sees it settled in the billing queue", context do
        {:ok, _invoices_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices")

        assert html =~ context.client.name
        assert html =~ "Paid"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  Criterion 7186 — Reminder includes confirm and reschedule actions

  Re-drives the lead-time trigger (as in criterion 7183) so the

  action links, rather than trusting a seeded row's shape.

        {:ok, reminders_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/reminders")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the test case to be used by
  tests that require setting up a connection.

  Such tests rely on `Phoenix.ConnTest` and also
  import other functionality to make it easier
  to build common data structures and query the data layer.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      # The default endpoint for testing
      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

      # Import conveniences for testing with connections
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.ConnTest
      import CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    {:ok, conn: Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()}
  end

  @doc """
  Setup helper that registers and logs in users.

      setup :register_and_log_in_user

  It stores an updated connection and a registered user in the
  test context.
  """
  def register_and_log_in_user(%{conn: conn} = context) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

    opts =
      context
      |> Map.take([:token_authenticated_at])
      |> Enum.into([])

    %{conn: log_in_user(conn, user, opts), user: user, scope: scope}
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given `user` into the `conn`.

  It returns an updated `conn`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, opts \\ []) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Users.generate_user_session_token(user)

    maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, opts[:token_authenticated_at])

    conn
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:user_token, token)
  end

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(_token, nil), do: nil

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) do
    CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story834.Criterion7170Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
  Criterion 7170 — Reassigning a job to another cleaner on the board
  updates that job's assignment immediately.

  Assumes each job card exposes a per-job cleaner-select control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-cleaner-select']`, `phx-change="reassign_job"`)
  since drag-and-drop isn't drivable through LiveViewTest.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the owner reassigns a job to another cleaner" do
    scenario "moving a job from Ana to Ben updates the assignment" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        scope = %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a Wednesday job is assigned to cleaner Ana", context do
        ana =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        ben =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ben-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Wednesday client"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: ana.id,
            scheduled_date: wednesday(),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[15:00:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{ana: ana, ben: ben, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the owner moves the job to cleaner Ben on the board", context do
        {:ok, view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        view
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-cleaner-select']")
        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(context.ben.id)})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :view, view)}
      end

      then_ "the job's assigned cleaner becomes Ben", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ben.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the job no longer appears under Ana", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ana.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp wednesday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    monday = Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
    Date.add(monday, 2)
  end
end
