defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false,
          email: "client#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    attrs = Enum.into(attrs, %{})
    start_time = Map.get(attrs, :start_time, ~T[09:00:00])

    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: start_time,
          # Some specs override `start_time` alone (e.g. pinning it to a
          # lead-time boundary) without overriding `end_time` — a fixed
          # `~T[11:00:00]` default would then land before an overridden
          # start_time and fail the "end after start" changeset check.
          end_time: default_end_time(start_time)
        })
      )

    # Notifications (story 837) — the automatic reminder trigger is a
    # periodic Oban-cron scan in production (see the background-jobs
    # ADR); nothing about creating a job through this fixture would
    # otherwise run that scan within a spec's lifetime. Running it here
    # is a no-op for every job outside its owning account's configured
    # lead-time window (and a no-op entirely for accounts that never
    # configured reminders), so it's safe for every other story's jobs
    # while making story 837's own boundary-timed fixtures deterministic.
    CleanerCrm.Notifications.send_due_reminders()

    job
  end

  # `given_` blocks bind `scope` from `user_scope_fixture/1` *before*
  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  # Two hours after `start_time`, unless that would wrap past midnight
  # (into an earlier clock time), in which case the day just ends there.
  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, 2 * 3600, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Client portal (stories 851, 852) — an already-established client
  # portal session.
  #
  # The magic-link exchange itself (`/portal/access/:token`) is covered
  # end-to-end by story 850's own specs. Downstream portal stories
  # whose subject is what a client can do once inside the portal seed
  # the session directly here instead of re-driving that exchange
  # every time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  # Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth` reads the client id from the
  # `:portal_client_id` session key (mirroring `:user_token` for staff
  # auth).
  def portal_session_fixture(client) do
    Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:portal_client_id, client.id)
  end

  # Reschedule/cancel policy (story 851) — the account's configured
  # notice window and fees.
  #
  # The client-facing decision (on-time, late, or same-day) is the
  # subject under test, so this only seeds the account's stated
  # policy, never a per-job fee outcome.
  def cancellation_policy_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, policy} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.set_cancellation_policy(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          notice_window_hours: 48,
          late_fee_cents: 2_500,
          same_day_fee_cents: 5_000
        })
      )

    policy
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story848.Criterion7215Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 848 — Get an instant quote from the public website
  Criterion 7215 — Building a quote with room counts shows a price
  with no contact info: a real price is shown from selecting a
  service type and room counts alone, before any name, email, or
  phone is entered.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the public quote form prices a per-room home before contact info is given" do
    scenario "building a quote with room counts shows a price with no contact info" do
      given_ "a business with a per-room rate card and a visitor on the public quote page",
             context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        Fixtures.rate_card_fixture(scope, %{
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 5000,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: 3000
        })

        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the visitor selects a service type, bedroom count, and bathroom count without entering a name, email, or phone",
            context do
        html =
          context.quote_live
          |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
            quote: %{pricing_model: "per_room", bedroom_count: 3, bathroom_count: 2}
          )
          |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "a real price computed from the rate card is displayed immediately", context do
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$210.00")
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='unsupported-quote-message']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story848.Criterion7221Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 848 — Get an instant quote from the public website
  Criterion 7221 — Instant quote price matches the later acceptance
  total: the number shown on the instant-quote calculator is exactly
  the number carried through to the accept-and-book step, with no
  added fees.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the instant quote total carries through unchanged to acceptance" do
    scenario "instant quote price matches the later acceptance total" do
      given_ "a visitor sees an instant quote total of $195 in integer cents", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        Fixtures.rate_card_fixture(scope, %{
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 6000,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: 3750
        })

        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book")

        quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
          quote: %{pricing_model: "per_room", bedroom_count: 2, bathroom_count: 2}
        )
        |> render_change()

        assert has_element?(quote_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$195.00")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "they proceed to the accept-and-book step without changing any selections", context do
        context.quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='lead-contact-form']",
          lead: %{name: "Dana Prescott", email: "dana@example.com", phone: "555-0142"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        path = assert_patch(context.quote_live)
        {:ok, accept_live, html} = live(context.conn, path)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{accept_live: accept_live, html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the total shown at acceptance is exactly $195 with no added fees", context do
        assert context.html =~ "$195.00"
        refute has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='added-fee']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

# Write BDD Specs: Accept a quote and book online with card on file

**Story ID**: 849
**Description**: As a cleaning client, I want to accept my quote online — pick a slot, agree to the cancellation policy, and put a card on file — so that booking is done in minutes and the price I saw is the price I'm charged. (Research: Jobber captures cards at quote acceptance; capturing policy agreement at booking is best practice; bait-and-switch pricing is a top category complaint — customer-side.md §1, §2)
**Component**: `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive` (live_context)

## What you're producing

These are specifications of acceptance criteria, not regression tests
of existing behavior. A scenario is a mechanical translation of the
criterion text into Given/When/Then driving the real surface — what
the criterion **says must be true**, not what the code happens to do
today.

**Failing on first run is the expected outcome.** Unsatisfied criteria
produce red specs; the next workflow step uses that red bar to drive
the implementation. You do **not** need the scenarios to pass for
this task to succeed.

**The evaluator is shape-only** — it parses, compiles, asserts
`use *.Spex.Case`, and asserts Given/When/Then steps exist. It does
**not** run `mix test`. Validation passing is not the same as
scenarios passing. Encode the criterion faithfully; let the implementer
worry about turning it green.

## Required reading — both layers

Read both knowledge layers before writing specs. **Project rules
override framework rules where they conflict.**

### Framework BDD knowledge (read via the `read_knowledge` MCP tool, under `bdd/spex/`)

- `bdd/spex/writing_a_spex.md` — file layout, module template, DSL
  syntax, step return values. **Essential — read first.**
- `bdd/spex/philosophy.md` — what Spex is and how it differs from
  regular tests.
- `bdd/spex/environment.md` — environment abstraction in steps.
- `bdd/spex/boundaries.md` — what `given_` / `when_` / `then_` can and
  can't do.
- `bdd/spex/shared_givens.md` — importing shared given blocks.
- `bdd/spex/recording_cassettes.md` — when and how to record HTTP
  cassettes.

### Project BDD knowledge (`.code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/`)

- `four_surfaces_quick_reference.md` — the four interaction surfaces
  in this codebase (MCP tool, HTTP, LiveView, filesystem) with
  one-line "I'm testing X → use surface Y" table and 30-second
  skeletons. **Read second.**
- `surfaces.md` — canonical skeletons per surface, deeper detail.
- `cassettes.md` — project-specific cassette conventions.

Failure modes that turn the spec into a self-fulfilling pass instead

- **`@tag :pending`, `@tag :skip`, or comment out scenarios that

  HTTP / MCP tool. Mocks make the spec a tautology.
- **Read the implementation and write its current behavior as the
  expectation.** Read the criterion; write the criterion. If the
  code doesn't match, that's information — surface it through a
  failing spec.

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.StripeWebhookController do
  @moduledoc """
  Public Stripe webhook endpoint (`POST /webhooks/stripe`) — the only
  place an invoice's payment status ever changes from a pending
  charge, per the payments-stripe ADR. Verification (real signature
  check in production, trusted as-is in test) happens inside
  `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1`, so this controller never
  branches on anything but its result.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing

  def create(conn, _params) do
    case Billing.receive_webhook(conn) do
      {:ok, _result} ->
        json(conn, %{received: true})

      {:error, _reason} ->
        conn
        |> put_status(:bad_request)
        |> json(%{error: "invalid_signature"})
    end
  end
end

  flow to cancellation policy and payment.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7233Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7233 — Client enters a valid card and the booking
  confirms: once the payment gateway accepts the card, it is stored
  on file and the booking is confirmed.

  As with story 836's card charges, the gateway's acceptance is only
  final once the provider confirms it via `POST /webhooks/stripe`
  (see `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1`) — submitting the card
  moves the booking to a pending-payment state; this spec's subject
  is the transition that follows the provider's confirmation.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the payment gateway accepting the card confirms the booking" do
    scenario "client enters a valid card and the booking confirms" do
      given_ "the client has agreed to the cancellation policy", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead = Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{total_cents: 19_500})

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
          booking: %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "09:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, accept_live: accept_live})}
      end

      when_ "the client enters a valid card and the payment gateway accepts it", context do
        context.accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']",
          booking: %{policy_agreed: "true", payment_method: "pm_card_visa"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        assert has_element?(context.accept_live, "[data-test='payment-pending']")

        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => "pi_test_booking_succeeded",
              "metadata" => %{"lead_id" => to_string(context.lead.id)}
            }
          }
        }

        response =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
          |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
          |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :webhook_response, response)}
      end

      then_ "the card is stored on file and the booking is confirmed", context do
        {:ok, accept_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{context.lead.acceptance_token}")

        assert html =~ "confirmed" or has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='booking-confirmed']")
        assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='booking-confirmed']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7236Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7236 — Confirmed booking appears for client and business
  with portal access: confirming converts the accepted quote into a
  scheduled job visible to both sides, and the client receives a
  confirmation containing a magic-link to their portal.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "confirming the booking makes the visit visible to both sides and grants portal access" do
    scenario "confirmed booking appears for client and business with portal access" do
      given_ "the booking has been confirmed with card on file", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead =
          Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{
            total_cents: 19_500,
            client_name: "Dana Prescott",
            client_email: "dana@example.com"
          })

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
          booking: %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "09:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']",
          booking: %{policy_agreed: "true", payment_method: "pm_card_visa"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => "pi_test_booking_confirmed",
              "metadata" => %{"lead_id" => to_string(lead.id)}
            }
          }
        }

        Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
        |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
        |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
        |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, account: account, owner_conn: owner_conn})}
      end

      when_ "the confirmation completes", context do
        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the visit appears as scheduled for both the business and the client, and the client receives a confirmation containing a magic-link to their portal",
            context do
        {:ok, _accept_live, client_html} =
          live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{context.lead.acceptance_token}")

        assert client_html =~ "scheduled" or client_html =~ "confirmed"

        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/schedule")
        assert has_element?(board_live, "[data-test]", context.lead.client_name)

        assert_email_sent(fn email ->
          email.to == [{"", context.lead.client_email}] and
            email.html_body =~ ~r{href="[^"]*portal[^"]*"}i
        end)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

# Write BDD Specs: See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal

**Story ID**: 850
**Description**: As a cleaning client, I want a portal showing my upcoming visits with the named, photo-identified cleaner assigned, plus my service history with checklist results and before/after photos, so that I know who is entering my home and can see exactly what I paid for. (Research: trust is the #1 gate — 73% of bad experiences trace to trust; Jobber's Client Hub shows assigned-team photos for this reason — customer-side.md §1, §2)
**Component**: `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive` (live_context)

## What you're producing

These are specifications of acceptance criteria, not regression tests
of existing behavior. A scenario is a mechanical translation of the
criterion text into Given/When/Then driving the real surface — what
the criterion **says must be true**, not what the code happens to do
today.

**Failing on first run is the expected outcome.** Unsatisfied criteria
produce red specs; the next workflow step uses that red bar to drive
the implementation. You do **not** need the scenarios to pass for
this task to succeed.

**The evaluator is shape-only** — it parses, compiles, asserts
`use *.Spex.Case`, and asserts Given/When/Then steps exist. It does
**not** run `mix test`. Validation passing is not the same as
scenarios passing. Encode the criterion faithfully; let the implementer
worry about turning it green.

## Required reading — both layers

Read both knowledge layers before writing specs. **Project rules
override framework rules where they conflict.**

### Framework BDD knowledge (read via the `read_knowledge` MCP tool, under `bdd/spex/`)

- `bdd/spex/writing_a_spex.md` — file layout, module template, DSL
  syntax, step return values. **Essential — read first.**
- `bdd/spex/philosophy.md` — what Spex is and how it differs from
  regular tests.
- `bdd/spex/environment.md` — environment abstraction in steps.
- `bdd/spex/boundaries.md` — what `given_` / `when_` / `then_` can and
  can't do.
- `bdd/spex/shared_givens.md` — importing shared given blocks.
- `bdd/spex/recording_cassettes.md` — when and how to record HTTP
  cassettes.

### Project BDD knowledge (`.code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/`)

- `four_surfaces_quick_reference.md` — the four interaction surfaces
  in this codebase (MCP tool, HTTP, LiveView, filesystem) with
  one-line "I'm testing X → use surface Y" table and 30-second
  skeletons. **Read second.**
- `surfaces.md` — canonical skeletons per surface, deeper detail.
- `cassettes.md` — project-specific cassette conventions.

## Component under test

Source: `lib/cleaner_crm_web/portal_live.ex` (couldn't read — open the file before writing specs to see the public API)

## Likely surface for this component

This component is a **live_context**. The most likely surface is
**LiveView (a user interacting with a page)**.

Pick by what the user (engineer or agent) would actually do, not by
component type alone — see
`.code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/four_surfaces_quick_reference.md`
for the full decision table and the 30-second skeleton.

## Acceptance criteria

### Criterion 7251: Client opens the portal via a valid magic link

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/850_see_my_visits_cleaner_and_proof-of-work_in_a_client_portal/criterion_7251_client_opens_the_portal_via_a_valid_magic_link_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7252: Expired or invalid magic link denies access

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/850_see_my_visits_cleaner_and_proof-of-work_in_a_client_portal/criterion_7252_expired_or_invalid_magic_link_denies_access_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7253: Upcoming visit shows the assigned cleaner's name and photo

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/850_see_my_visits_cleaner_and_proof-of-work_in_a_client_portal/criterion_7253_upcoming_visit_shows_the_assigned_cleaners_name_and_photo_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7254: Reassigning the cleaner updates what the client sees

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/850_see_my_visits_cleaner_and_proof-of-work_in_a_client_portal/criterion_7254_reassigning_the_cleaner_updates_what_the_client_sees_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7255: Unassigned upcoming visit shows a placeholder

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/850_see_my_visits_cleaner_and_proof-of-work_in_a_client_portal/criterion_7255_unassigned_upcoming_visit_shows_a_placeholder_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7256: Completed visit in history shows checklist and before/after photos

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/850_see_my_visits_cleaner_and_proof-of-work_in_a_client_portal/criterion_7256_completed_visit_in_history_shows_checklist_and_beforeafter_photos_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7257: Portal proof-of-work matches the invoice's evidence

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/850_see_my_visits_cleaner_and_proof-of-work_in_a_client_portal/criterion_7257_portal_proof-of-work_matches_the_invoices_evidence_spex.exs`

## Procedure

Write **one** spec file per criterion, then **stop** for validation.
The evaluator runs after each session — it checks file existence,
parses, compiles via `Code.string_to_quoted/2`, asserts `use` of
`CleanerCrmSpex.Case`, and asserts at least one scenario with
Given/When/Then steps. If validation fails, next-session feedback
tells you exactly what's wrong.

For each criterion:

1. Create the spec file at the path shown above.
2. Module name under the `CleanerCrmSpex` namespace.
3. `use CleanerCrmSpex.Case` (NOT `<App>Web.ConnCase` directly —
   the case template wires up SexySpex + ConnTest + LiveViewTest +
   DB sandbox).
4. Drive the real interaction surface from `given_` / `when_` /
   `then_` steps. Never call context functions or `Repo` directly.
   Never read the DB from `then_`.
5. Run `mix compile` to verify.
6. **Stop and wait for validation** before starting the next spec.

## Do not

Failure modes that turn the spec into a self-fulfilling pass instead
of a faithful encoding of the criterion:

- **Soften the assertion to match current behavior.** If the criterion
  says 401, assert 401 — not `assert conn.status in [200, 401]`
  because the code returns 200 today.
- **Fabricate rules or criteria.** Only write scenarios for the rules
  and criteria already on the story. If something feels
  under-specified, surface the question — don't invent a rule.
- **`@tag :pending`, `@tag :skip`, or comment out scenarios that
  fail.** A failing scenario is the point. Tagging it out hides the
  signal the implementer needs.
- **Pre-seed in `given_` what the SUT should produce.** If the
  criterion says "creating a Foo also creates a Bar", `when_`
  triggers the action and `then_` asserts both side effects.
  Don't `given_` the Bar into existence.
- **Stub or mock the surface under test.** Drive the real LiveView /
  HTTP / MCP tool. Mocks make the spec a tautology.
- **Read the implementation and write its current behavior as the
  expectation.** Read the criterion; write the criterion. If the
  code doesn't match, that's information — surface it through a
  failing spec.

If a criterion is genuinely untestable, contradicts another, or is
ambiguous, **stop and flag it** rather than fudging the spec to fit.

## Reference files

- Case template: `test/support/cleaner_crm_spex_case.ex` — defines
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Case`.
- Boundary: `test/spex/cleaner_crm_spex.ex`.
- Shared givens: `test/support/shared_givens.ex`.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story850.Criterion7251Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 850 — See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  Criterion 7251 — Client opens the portal via a valid magic link: the
  portal opens showing upcoming visits and service history, with no
  password required.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a valid magic-link token opens the client's portal" do
    scenario "client opens the portal via a valid magic link" do
      given_ "a client has been sent a magic-link token for their portal", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})
        session = Fixtures.portal_magic_link_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, session: session})}
      end

      when_ "the client follows the link", context do
        access_conn = get(context.conn, ~p"/portal/access/#{context.session.token}")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :access_conn, access_conn)}
      end

      then_ "the portal opens showing their upcoming visits and service history without requiring a password",
            context do
        assert redirected_to(context.access_conn) == ~p"/portal"

        {:ok, portal_live, _html} = context.access_conn |> recycle() |> live(~p"/portal")

        assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='upcoming-visits']")
        assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='service-history']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story850.Criterion7252Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 850 — See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  Criterion 7252 — Expired or invalid magic link denies access:
  access is denied and the client is offered a way to request a
  fresh link.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "an expired magic-link token denies portal access" do
    scenario "expired or invalid magic link denies access" do
      given_ "a client's magic-link token has expired", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})

        session =
          Fixtures.portal_magic_link_fixture(client, %{
            expires_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -3600, :second)
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, session: session})}
      end

      when_ "the client follows the link", context do
        access_conn = get(context.conn, ~p"/portal/access/#{context.session.token}")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :access_conn, access_conn)}
      end

      then_ "access to the portal is denied and the client is offered a way to request a fresh link",
            context do
        refute redirected_to(context.access_conn, 302) == ~p"/portal"

        html = Phoenix.ConnTest.html_response(context.access_conn, 200)
        assert html =~ ~r/expired|invalid/i
        assert html =~ ~r/request a new link|request a fresh link/i

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  Story 850 — See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  Criterion 7253 — Upcoming visit shows the assigned cleaner's name
  and photo alongside the date/time.

        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story850.Criterion7254Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 850 — See my visits, cleaner, and proof-of-work in a client portal
  Criterion 7254 — Reassigning the cleaner updates what the client
  sees: the next time the portal is viewed, it shows the newly
  assigned cleaner.

  Reassignment is driven through the real dispatch board
  (`ScheduleLive.Board`, covered end-to-end by story 834's own
  reassignment specs), not seeded directly, since the board's
  cleaner-select is the actual mechanism that changes a job's
  assignment.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "reassigning a visit's cleaner is reflected the next time the portal is viewed" do
    scenario "reassigning the cleaner updates what the client sees" do
      given_ "a client's upcoming visit currently shows Cleaner A", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
        cleaner_a = Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(scope, account, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Morgan Blake"})
        job = Fixtures.job_fixture(scope, client, %{cleaner_id: cleaner_a.id})
        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(portal_conn, ~p"/portal")
        assert has_element?(portal_live, "[data-test='visit-#{job.id}']", cleaner_a.name)

        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           scope: scope,
           account: account,
           cleaner_a: cleaner_a,
           client: client,
           job: job,
           portal_conn: portal_conn,
           owner_conn: owner_conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "the business reassigns the visit to Cleaner B", context do
        cleaner_b = Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{name: "Sam Okafor"})

        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-cleaner-select']")
        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(cleaner_b.id)})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :cleaner_b, cleaner_b)}
      end

      then_ "the client's portal shows Cleaner B's name and photo the next time it is viewed",
            context do
        {:ok, portal_live, _html} = live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal")

        assert has_element?(
                 portal_live,
                 "[data-test='visit-#{context.job.id}']",
                 context.cleaner_b.name
               )

        refute has_element?(
                 portal_live,
                 "[data-test='visit-#{context.job.id}']",
                 context.cleaner_a.name
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7156Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7156 — Invoice shows the job's proof-of-work
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "attaching a completed job's proof-of-work to its invoice" do
    scenario "invoice shows the job's proof-of-work" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a job was completed with a finished checklist and before/after photos", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)
        invoice = Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{amount: job.agreed_price})

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, invoice: invoice})}
      end

      when_ "the invoice for that job is opened", context do
        {:ok, invoice_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices/#{context.invoice.id}")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{invoice_live: invoice_live, invoice_html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the completed checklist is attached to the invoice", context do
        assert context.invoice_html =~ "Kitchen counters wiped down"
        assert context.invoice_html =~ "Bathrooms sanitized"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the before/after photos are attached to the invoice as dispute evidence", context do
        assert has_element?(context.invoice_live, "[data-test='proof-of-work-photo']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

I found another agent already working in that same file on stories 851/852 (adding `portal_session_fixture/1` and `cancellation_policy_fixture/2`) — I kept my additions distinctly named and verified both sets coexist without conflict.
